compatibility_evidence.text: Win executes inline classic scripts and fetched external classic scripts in document order in a separate W JavaScript interpreter instance for each page/tab. Failed downloads and script exceptions produce a status diagnostic and do not prevent later scripts from running. The resource queue may fetch scripts concurrently, but execution waits for earlier script elements. Scripts use the fully parsed document; parser-blocking execution, `async` and `defer` scheduling are not modeled. `DOMContentLoaded` fires once on Document after the initial script queue finishes, with `readyState` set to `interactive`; it does not wait for unrelated image downloads. `load` fires once on Window after all initial resources finish, with `readyState` set to `complete`.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: This is an implementation of W's bounded JavaScript language subset, not an ECMAScript-complete browser engine. Supported language features include `let`/`const`, function/global `var` hoisting, ordinary and async functions/closures, synchronous and async arrows, method-call receivers (`this`), objects and arrays, property access/assignment, conditionals, loops, labelled blocks/loops with targeted `break`/`continue`, arithmetic, strict comparisons, `typeof`, and exceptions. Arrows retain the enclosing receiver; global `this` and sloppy receiver substitution/boxing remain unsupported. See [W's runtime contract](../../w/docs/projects/javascript.md). Unsupported syntax/operations produce a diagnostic, including generators, async methods, and arbitrary-precision BigInt arithmetic. RegExp literals/constructors, exec/test and String.replace implement a bounded UTF-16 subset with explicit unsupported features; see [the RegExp contract](../../w/docs/projects/javascript_regexp.md). Bounded classes support constructors, prototype/static methods, inheritance, super-constructor calls and instanceof; accessors/private fields/super-property access remain outside the class subset. Bounded 64-bit BigInt arithmetic preserves exact bits and rejects overflow. Bounded binding patterns/defaults/rest, spread, optional chaining, and selected native constructors are now supported. Bounded abstract equality (`==`/`!=`) performs ordinary primitive conversion; Addition and bitwise operators implement bounded ordinary primitive/numeric conversion; other arithmetic coercion and many standard built-ins remain outside the subset. Iterative logical, comma, conditional, binary and statement-tail evaluation avoids artificial AST recursion while retaining execution and call-depth limits. For-in enumerates descriptor/prototype keys with mutation rules; `in` uses descriptor lookup and explicit native presence hooks. JSON script data is ignored. Module scripts use a bounded asynchronous source loader connected to W's [acyclic module foundation](../../w/docs/projects/javascript_modules.md), with same-origin named imports, live named variable/function/class exports and top-level await. Pending module evaluation lets Fetch/timers/Promise jobs advance and delays the initial DOMContentLoaded/load lifecycle; rejection is cached and reported without replaying module bodies. The bounded scheduling and storage APIs below are available, along with same-origin `fetch` and Promise-based `Response.text()` / `Response.arrayBuffer()` / `Response.json()` subsets. See [web application execution](web-app-compatibility.md) for wasm, canvas, and binary interfaces. XHR, location assignment, and access to W/OS capabilities from page code remain unavailable.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Array callback methods now include generic `every`, `forEach`, `map`, `filter`,
`find`, `findIndex`, `findLast`, `findLastIndex`, `reduce` and `reduceRight`.
They preserve callback order, sparse/inherited properties, live mutation and
shared execution limits; custom species and Symbol hooks remain unsupported.
See the [array iteration contract](../../w/docs/projects/javascript_array.md#callback-iteration).
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`String(value)` supports bounded ordinary object conversion and Error
stringification; wrapper construction and Symbol hooks remain unsupported.
`parseFloat` and `Number.parseFloat` share a bounded decimal-prefix parser with
ECMAScript whitespace, signed zero, Infinity and correctly rounded binary64
results. These do not imply general implicit coercion.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The default script/task budget is 1,000,000 shared JavaScript/Wasm steps.
`--execution-budget N` explicitly selects 1–200,000,000 steps for ordinary native
pages and new tabs. The same cap covers script/module entry, event dispatch,
timers, animation batches and microtask checkpoints; reentrant imports do not
refill fuel. Suspended async tasks conserve their original budget. Native Fetch
settlement retains its independent 100,000-step entry bound. Isolated interactive
workers receive the selected budget; isolated headless dumps reject custom budgets
until policy forwarding exists. Higher budgets can block the
parent UI for seconds; they permit measured experiments, not responsiveness claims.
All heap/source/stack/resource limits remain enforced independently.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `clearTimeout`, and `clearInterval` are available on
the global scope and Window. Callbacks must be functions; source-string timers
are rejected. Numeric delays are clamped to 0–2,147,483,647 ms (intervals have a
1 ms minimum); delay coercion is not implemented. Timers accept up to three extra
callback arguments and invoke ordinary callbacks with Window as `this`. There
are at most 256 active timers. Timer IDs are unique within a realm, and either
clear function can cancel either timer kind.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The runtime provides `new Promise(executor)`, `Promise.resolve`,
`Promise.reject`, `then`, `catch`, `finally`, and `queueMicrotask`. Executors run
synchronously; reactions run at checkpoints. Settlement is first-call-wins,
chains adopt native promises and generic thenables, and retained jobs participate
in garbage collection. Resolution reads `then` synchronously and queues its call;
shared resolving capabilities enforce first-call-wins even with reentrancy.
`finally` awaits cleanup and preserves the original result unless cleanup fails.
`Promise.all`, `race`, and `allSettled` accept the supported array/string
iterables, preserve result ordering, and assimilate thenables. Custom iterators,
`Promise.any`, generic constructors/species, and unhandled-rejection events remain
unsupported.
Async functions and top-level module await use suspended
W generator stacks resumed by Promise jobs. Suspension is bounded to 32 tasks,
8 MiB of stack storage and a separate retained-root quota; fuel is conserved
across checkpoints. Stop/navigation unwind suspended native temporaries and
invalidate queued resumptions before freeing host records. Await assimilates
thenables through the same Promise resolution mechanism.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Each owner is bounded to 1 MiB and 1,024 entries across its origins; keys and
values are at most 64 KiB each. Quota failures throw `QuotaExceededError` and leave
the old value intact. Strings use the browser binding's bounded primitive string
conversion. Named-property storage access, storage events,
full Web IDL coercion, and new-tab session copying are not implemented.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`fetch(url, options)` and `window.fetch(url, options)` support HTTP(S) to the document's own
scheme/host/effective-port origin. Relative references resolve against its final
URL. Cross-origin redirects are rejected before the foreign request; local files
and CORS requests are unavailable. Options may supply `method`, `body`, native `signal`, and a plain data record
of Content-Type/Accept headers. Bodies are bounded to 64 KiB, accept strings or
copied BufferSource views and preserve embedded NUL bytes. GET/HEAD reject
bodies; CONNECT/TRACE/TRACK are forbidden. Unsupported headers/options are
rejected rather than silently ignored. Binary request framing, redirect behavior
and exact limits are described in [network compatibility](network-compatibility.md). Loading uses cancellable child processes and existing deadlines.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The returned native Promise fulfills with `status`, `ok`, `url`, `bodyUsed`, and
`text()`, `arrayBuffer()`, and `json()`. HTTP error statuses still fulfill; transport failures reject.
`text()`, `arrayBuffer()` and `json()` return Promises and share a single-use body. Bodies
are limited to 4 MiB each; `text()` additionally requires valid UTF-8 and at most
64 KiB. Binary bodies are preserved byte-for-byte. Encoding replacement for text,
streaming, blob helpers, response headers, and XHR remain unsupported.
`json()` accepts up to 64 KiB, uses forgiving UTF-8 decoding, then strict bounded
JSON parsing, with `SyntaxError` rejection and consumed-on-failure semantics. A page allows three
concurrent fetches, 64 requests over its lifetime, and 4 MiB of retained body
bytes. Responses remain owned until document teardown. `AbortController` exposes a
stable branded `signal`, exact `reason`, `aborted`, `throwIfAborted`, `onabort`
and function-valued abort listeners. Native observers cancel/reap Fetch workers
before JS listeners run. Aborting after fulfillment rejects unread response
bodies. At most 256 controllers are retained per realm and 1,024 active listeners
per signal. Signal composition/timeouts, full prototypes and DOMException classes
remain unsupported. Navigation/tab closure
cancel outstanding workers before freeing their realm.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
State supports null, top-level undefined, strings, booleans, finite numbers other
than negative zero, and dense JSON-compatible plain object/array trees. Each
snapshot is independently cloned, bounded to 64 KiB, 32 levels and 4,096 object
identities. Unsupported values, cycles/shared object references, accessors,
`toJSON`, sparse arrays and extra array properties throw `DataCloneError` before
mutation. This is a storage subset, not general structured clone. General URL
argument coercion, complete `go` Web IDL conversion, scrollRestoration, hashchange,
navigation assignment and the Navigation API remain unsupported.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The additional host surface includes `location.search`, mutable
`URLSearchParams`, viewport globals and resize events, `getBoundingClientRect`,
client/offset dimensions, and live computed padding/font-size/pointer-events/flex-direction reads through
`getComputedStyle`. VisualViewport, general computed styles, and navigation
assignment are not implemented.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Each list has at most 1,024 pairs and 65,536 UTF-16 units across names/values;
input strings and serialized output are each limited to 65,536 units. A realm
retains at most 256 parameter objects and 524,288 combined name/value units until
document teardown. Failed construction releases its native allocations. Mutation
and sort budget/quota failures preserve the existing list, apart from mutations
already performed by user conversion functions or callbacks. Serialization can
exceed its limit even when the unencoded list fits. These are terminal host
limits, not standard URL API exceptions.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
This is a standalone parameter-list subset: the `URL` class and live
`URL.searchParams` association, general iterable initializers, Symbol hooks,
`entries`/`keys`/`values` iterator objects, and complete Web IDL reflection remain
unsupported. `forEach` is the supported iteration interface. The existing
History API can consume `'?' + params.toString()` for same-origin routing.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: `document`, `window.document`, and `document.body` expose stable element wrappers. The limited `window`/`globalThis` object is distinct from Document and has its own event registrations. `window.document === document` and `globalThis === window`; the Window wrapper is not the interpreter's lexical global environment, so global declarations do not automatically become Window properties.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
- `getElementById`, `querySelector`, and `querySelectorAll` (a static array) using Win's supported CSS selectors.
- Element `matches(selector)` returns a boolean; `closest(selector)` checks the element and then its ancestors, returning the nearest matching wrapper or null, including in detached trees. These and the query methods share filtered nth-child selectors and forgiving `:is()`/`:where()` lists. An invalid or unsupported strict selector list throws a catchable object with `name: 'SyntaxError'` and a `message`, even on an empty tree; native DOMException prototypes are not implemented. A valid forgiving list with no surviving branches simply matches nothing.
- `textContent`, `value`, `id`, `className`, `checked`, and `hidden` properties; `document.title` and `document.readyState`.
- `getAttribute`, `setAttribute`, and `removeAttribute`.
- Input/textarea `selectionStart`, `selectionEnd`, `selectionDirection`, and `setSelectionRange` use UTF-16 offsets with clamping. Native focus, editing and selection task events remain incomplete.
- `createElement`, `createTextNode`, `appendChild`, `replaceChildren`, and `remove`. Element `replaceChildren` accepts nodes and primitive strings with preflight hierarchy validation; Document and DocumentFragment variants are absent. Detached nodes remain owned until the page is freed, so retained wrappers remain safe.
- `classList.add`, `.remove`, `.toggle`, and `.contains` with one class token per call.
- `style.cssText`, `.color`, `.backgroundColor`, `.display`, `.fontSize`, `.fontWeight`, `.width`, `.height`, `.margin`, `.padding`, `.border`, `.flex`, `.flexGrow`, `.flexShrink`, `.flexBasis`, `.flexDirection`, `.pointerEvents`, and `.justifyContent` reads/writes. `getPropertyValue`, `getPropertyPriority`, `setProperty`, and `removeProperty` operate on supported CSS property names; `setProperty` accepts an optional `important` priority. Reads return specified inline values, not computed cascade values. `cssText` normalizes declaration order, separators, and spacing. Invalid individual property assignments leave existing declarations unchanged; replacing `cssText` keeps only valid supported declarations. The interface does not implement general computed styles, stylesheet rule APIs, or complete CSSStyleDeclaration enumeration/serialization; limited computed padding/font-size/pointer-events/flex-direction reads are listed above.
- `addEventListener`, `removeEventListener`, function-valued `on...` properties, and inline event attributes for the supported language subset. Listener registration accepts a boolean capture argument or an options object with `capture`, `once`, and `passive`; removal matches the callback, event type, and capture flag.
- `console.log`, `.warn`, and `.error` retain their first argument in a bounded per-page console buffer (the last 32 entries, at most 4 KiB each). A console panel is not yet provided.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: Native property hooks read and write the document synchronously: an ancestor `textContent` read immediately observes a descendant assignment without an intervening host call. Inline style mutations are synchronous too. Embedded stylesheet text changes and stylesheet insertion, removal, and reordering reconcile active sheets at evaluation/host boundaries. Existing linked stylesheets are retained by node and URL. Resource discovery reconciles connected scripts, links, and images and changed resource URLs during browser polling. Newly connected classic scripts execute once per node, including after initial page load; removing and reinserting an executed script does not replay it. Detached pending scripts are skipped. Discovery and execution are bounded and polled, not the complete HTML script preparation algorithm. `innerHTML`, live collections, attribute/property reflection beyond the listed fields, DOM prototypes, and mutation observers are not implemented. W supplies host descriptor/prototype hooks, but this does not expose the full JavaScript accessor or DOM interface surface. Node `tagName` uses the parser's lowercase spelling.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The event behavior follows the supported portions of the
[DOM event dispatch model](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-event-dispatch).
Listeners and property/inline handlers receive their current event target as
`this`; arrows keep their lexical receiver. Connected-node event paths include
Window after Document, while detached trees do not reach either. Window and
Document retain separate listener registrations, and page load targets Window.
`new Event(type, options)` and `dispatchEvent(event)` support synthetic dispatch,
including reentrancy, event identity, nested dispatch and the same listener rules.
Core event fields are read-only; synthetic events have `isTrusted:false`. Nested
dispatch checkpoints run after the outermost invocation. Listener objects with
`handleEvent`, listener abort options, and shadow DOM event paths remain unsupported.
Supported property/inline handlers interleave with listeners in registration
order, as detailed below. Core event fields use native read-only descriptors.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: Each script/callback dispatch defaults to a 1,000,000-step interpreter budget, including charged DOM traversals; depth is limited to 128. A script source is limited to 256 KiB and a realm retains at most 512 script ASTs, 100,000 runtime heap values, 1,024 node wrappers, and 1,024 registered listeners. The document has at most 20,000 nodes; DOM text/attribute strings and listener type names are limited to 64 KiB and copied DOM mutation data (including listener type names) has a conservative cumulative 4 MiB allocation budget. Removed/once listeners release their registrations and callback roots after dispatch; removals outside dispatch reclaim slots immediately. Interpreter limit failures terminate the dispatch, while ordinary callback exceptions allow later listeners to run. Appending a node cannot create cycles or exceed document depth limits. Reads of `textContent` return at most 64 KiB. These are deterministic limits, not resumable execution or a standards-compliant sandbox.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: Tests in `win/tests/script_test.w` cover timer ordering/cancellation/bounds, microtask checkpoints, storage reload/origin/tab isolation and quotas, mutation, selector identity, insertion, styles/classes, event phases and options, propagation/cancelation, form input values, inline handlers, lifecycle, console storage, execution/allocation bounds, failure recovery, and realm isolation. The HTTP resource fixture checks ordered external execution and download-failure isolation. `win/fixtures/standards.html` and the browser integration suite exercise capture/once listeners and canceled form navigation together with expanded CSS selectors and colors. `win/tests/cssom_test.w` additionally covers synchronous DOM properties, inline CSSOM operations, stylesheet mutations, distinct Window events, receiver identity, and separate DOM/content load readiness. W's merged runtime foundation expands the subset described above; these tests do not establish full ECMAScript or DOM conformance.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text: The standards command `./win/build standards` runs a [bounded upstream Test262 runtime profile](../../w/tests/javascript/test262/README.md) in addition to static WPT rendering. Labelled control flow includes nested/chained labels, outward jumps, and finally propagation; Annex B labelled function declarations remain unsupported.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
The runtime provides bounded `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify`, preserving UTF-16
strings (including escaped NUL/lone surrogates), strict number/syntax validation,
property ordering, toJSON, cycle and BigInt errors. Revivers/replacers and broader
coercion are outside this subset; see W's runtime contract for exact limits.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Live HTML Node tree access, child lists, Text data and bounded node creation/moves
are described in [the DOM tree contract](dom-tree.md). Native property presence
uses explicit hooks and does not invoke getters or force layout. Mouse pointer
input and capture use an ordered bounded native queue; native and programmatic
focus synchronize activeElement, focus events and UTF-16 text selections.
Ordered portable KEY/CHAR/NAV records now deliver logical keyboard events and
cancelable beforeinput followed by input for native edits. Unicode input and
Backspace pass through the unchanged mobile host into its wasm field; the hidden
textarea resets after each edit. Unknown hardware keys report Unidentified.
Bounded preedit snapshots produce compositionstart/update/end; the backend
provides no committed payload at PREEDIT_END, so compositionend.data is empty
and later CHAR events perform the commit. Full platform IME behavior remains
unsupported; focused tests do not establish X11/Windows key translation parity.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Supported nullable `on*` handler properties now register in listener order.
Replacing a callback keeps its slot; clearing and re-enabling moves it to a new
slot. Inline attribute changes invalidate the compiled handler, and a returned
false value cancels cancelable events. The implementation covers the names in
`win/src/win/event_handlers.w`, including the onclick/oninput/onsubmit properties
used by the pinned framework. Window ErrorEvent extra arguments, body-to-window
handler aliases and inline form/name scope remain unsupported.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Ordinary functions provide shared `call`, `apply` and `bind`, including bounded
bound construction. Strict/non-simple functions provide unmapped arguments,
and generic array-like `slice` uses property presence before reading elements.
Sloppy mapped arguments remain unsupported. Shared String prototype casing uses
Unicode 12.1 mappings with default final-sigma handling and resource bounds; see
[W’s casing contract](../../w/docs/projects/javascript_string_case.md).
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Tab and Shift+Tab traverse links, form controls and explicit `tabindex` elements.
Positive indices sort first by value, with DOM order breaking ties; zero/native
entries follow current DOM order. Negative indices remain programmatically
focusable but are omitted from sequential traversal. Hidden and disabled content
are skipped; visible descendants may override inherited `visibility:hidden`.
`pointer-events:none` does not remove keyboard access.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Traversal and Enter-link activation run through the ordered native input path,
including isolated workers. Canceling keydown suppresses the default; link
activation dispatches a cancelable click and observes a handler's changed href
before navigating. Focus rings and reveal use the final box or inline-run
geometry. Native new-tab link targets work; isolated new-tab transport is still
unsupported. Traversal wraps within the document and is bounded to 20,000 nodes
and depth 128.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
These changes improve keyboard access. Linux AT-SPI/screen-reader integration,
ARIA semantic trees, shadow/iframe focus scopes, radio-group roving focus and
complete platform keyboard/IME support remain open. Tests cover native and
isolated traversal/activation and actual rendered focus pixels.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Win now applies embedded and linked author stylesheets and inline declarations.
Stylesheet order follows document order even when external requests finish in a
different order. Each declaration competes by `!important`, selector specificity,
and source order; inline declarations outrank normal stylesheet declarations.
Specificity is compared as a tuple rather than a packed integer. Declarations
are validated before competing, so an invalid later value does not erase a valid
winner. Font-relative lengths resolve after the cascade selects the final font
size. Inherited text properties flow to descendants, and supported properties
accept `inherit`, `initial`, and `unset`. The implementation uses W's owned,
bounded CSS tokenizer/parser; unsupported selectors and conditional at-rules are
ignored rather than matching every element.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Pseudo-classes include `:root`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:only-child`,
`:first-of-type`, `:last-of-type`, `:only-of-type`, `:link`, `:checked`, `:disabled`,
`:not()`, `:is()`, and `:where()`. `:nth-child()`, `:nth-last-child()`,
`:nth-of-type()`, and `:nth-last-of-type()` accept integer `an+b` expressions,
integers, `odd`, and `even`, including negative coefficients and offsets.
Coefficients and offsets are limited to magnitude 1,000,000,000.
`:nth-child(An+B of S)` and `:nth-last-child(An+B of S)` count only siblings
matching the selector list `S`, including the candidate itself; filters may use
supported complex selectors. Their specificity includes the most specific filter
branch, even if that branch does not match the candidate. The `of` clause is not
valid for `:nth-of-type()` or `:nth-last-of-type()`.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`:is()` and `:where()` use forgiving lists: invalid or unsupported branches are
discarded, contribute no specificity, and an empty surviving list matches nothing.
`:is()` uses the maximum surviving branch specificity; `:where()` contributes zero.
Ordinary selector lists, `:not()` arguments, and nth-child filters are strict:
one invalid branch rejects the entire list, including a whole stylesheet rule.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Pseudo-elements, interaction pseudo-classes such as `:hover`, namespaces and CSS nesting are not
implemented. `@media` supports screen/all and conjunctions of `min-width`
and `max-width` lengths in px/em/rem (media em/rem use the initial 18px size);
unsupported queries (including print) do not apply. Media queries
are re-evaluated on layout, including viewport resize.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
- `color`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `font-style`, `text-decoration`,
  `white-space`, `text-align`, `line-height`, `display`, `visibility`, and
  inherited `pointer-events:auto/none`.
- `width`, `height`, `max-width`, `box-sizing`, `margin`, `padding`, and their
  four physical side longhands. Horizontal auto margins center or right-align
  constrained block boxes.
- Solid `background`/`background-color`, `border`, `border-width`, `border-style`, and
  `border-color` for block boxes.
- `gap`, `column-gap`, `flex-direction`, `flex`, `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`,
  `flex-basis`, `flex-wrap`, `align-items`, `align-self`, `justify-content`, and `grid-template-columns` for the
  limited flex/grid layouts described below.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Lengths accept px, em, rem, vw, vh, vmin, and vmax values, including fractional and exponent numeric
syntax and case-insensitive units. Box geometry retains floating-point lengths;
font rasterization and some image/text placement still use integer metrics.
Width and max-width also accept percentages. Font-size percentages are
relative to the inherited font size. Line height accepts pixels, em/rem,
percentages, unitless inherited multipliers, normal, and inherit; values smaller
than the font metrics currently keep the natural line height. Used lengths are
bounded to a magnitude of 1,000,000 pixels; font rasterization uses bounded strike
sizes. `calc()` supports nested parentheses, compatible addition/subtraction,
number multiplication, and division by a nonzero number. Percentages remain
symbolic until the supported property supplies its reference dimension. Mixed
length/percentage calculations work for width, max-width, flex-basis, font-size,
and line-height; they do not add percentage support to other properties.
Viewport units use the browser viewport, independent of content layout width.
`min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, `env()`, dimensional cancellation, and small/large/
dynamic viewport variants remain unsupported.
Colors accept `rgb()`/`rgba()` and `hsl()`/`hsla()` in comma-separated and
space-separated forms, with slash alpha in space-separated forms. Hues accept
unitless degrees, `deg`, `grad`, `rad`, and `turn`, including wrapping negative
angles. Alpha accepts numbers and percentages. RGB and alpha channels are clamped
to their valid ranges. HSL saturation and lightness accept percentages, or numbers
in space-separated syntax, and are clamped to 0–100 before conversion. Color math
uses float32; the native 8-bit canvas rounds RGB channels at the paint boundary
to avoid half-byte GL interpolation differences, while preserving computed
values and alpha; this can differ by a channel level from float RGB composition
for translucent or antialiased paint. Out-of-gamut Color 4 mapping is not implemented. Colors also accept
3/4/6/8-digit hex, transparent, and the classic CSS palette (black,
white, gray/grey, silver, red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, navy, teal,
maroon, olive, lime, aqua/cyan, and fuchsia/magenta). Invalid color declarations
leave earlier valid declarations effective. Relative colors, other color spaces,
gradients and background images are not implemented.
Functional colors apply to `color`, `background`, `background-color`,
`border-color`, and the `border` shorthand. Space-separated RGB/HSL forms accept
`none` for any channel (including alpha), rendered as zero; comma-separated forms
reject it. Missing-component preservation for interpolation and computed color
serialization is not implemented.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Uniform borders support `solid`, `none`, and `hidden` styles, pixel/em/rem widths
with fractional layout geometry, and `thin`/`medium`/`thick` (1/3/5 pixels).
Border painting currently uses whole-pixel widths.
Width and style cascade independently: a width alone does not enable painting.
The shorthand accepts supported components in any order and resets omitted
components to medium width, none style, and `currentColor`. Invalid or duplicate
components reject the whole declaration. Each component competes independently
with longhands and `!important`. Omitted border colors and explicit `currentColor`
in `border`/`border-color` follow the final computed text color. Per-side borders,
multiple longhand values and other line styles remain unsupported.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`display:flex` in row direction supports nonnegative `flex-grow`/`flex-shrink`
factors and `flex-basis` lengths (px/em/rem), percentages, `auto`, and `content`.
The `flex` shorthand accepts one to three components, `none`, and CSS-wide
keywords; omitted grow/shrink factors are 1 and omitted basis is zero. Initial
values remain 0 1 auto. Invalid shorthand values preserve earlier declarations
atomically; each expanded longhand participates in the cascade and inline CSSOM.
Basis percentages resolve against the container, `auto` uses a specified width
or content, and `content` ignores the item's specified width. Basis sizing
respects `box-sizing`.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
Horizontal auto margins consume remaining positive space before
`justify-content`. Row alignment supports `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`,
`space-between`, `space-around`, and `space-evenly`, with gaps included and safe
start fallback for distributed alignment on overflow. Controls and decoded
images contribute their own intrinsic dimensions;
failed or missing images use alt-text sizing. Descendant text measurement is approximate,
rather than a complete CSS min/max-content algorithm.
Percentage widths and max-widths resolve against the flex container once. Column
containers support `justify-content` against a definite height and horizontal
`align-items`/`align-self`, including horizontal auto margins. Auto-width column
items stretch by default, or use bounded intrinsic widths for other alignments.
Column containers with definite heights also resolve grow/shrink and flex-basis
using the shared flexible-length allocator. Percentage bases use a definite main
size; indefinite columns use content sizing. Final allocated heights reach nested
layout before painting and hit testing.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
`flex-wrap:wrap` collects row lines using outer hypothetical sizes, including
margins, padding, borders and gaps, before resolving flexible lengths separately
for each line. Oversized items occupy a line; exact fits stay on the current line.
Each line applies its own auto margins and `justify-content` distribution.
`align-items` supports `stretch`, `flex-start`, `flex-end`, and `center`;
`align-self` adds `auto`. Row alignment uses the line's outer item heights,
or the definite container height for nowrap. Wrapped rows implement the default
`align-content:stretch` behavior for positive extra height. Stretch changes an
auto-height item's border box and reruns nested layout against that final height.
Alignment translates descendant runs, boxes and fragment anchors together to
keep painting and hit testing consistent.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:

column tokens or `repeat(N, ...)`, wrapping later children into rows. Gap separates
rows/tracks. Column wrapping, wrap-reverse, baseline alignment,
vertical auto margins, explicit align-content, explicit min-width, intrinsic sizing keywords in flex-basis, proportional/fixed grid track
sizes, grid placement, and complete intrinsic sizing algorithms remain unsupported.
Grid alignment remains unsupported.

compatibility_evidence.text:

auto dimensions. Nested fixed boxes use the viewport independently. Painting,
hit testing, CSSOM geometry and focus reveal share the same scroll-adjusted
coordinates. `fixed_layout_test.w` and `fixed_layout_integration.py` cover geometry,
resize, scroll and full-viewport native paint. Generic containers no longer receive
synthetic margins; semantic paragraph/heading/list defaults remain.

compatibility_evidence.text:
- At most 32 cookies, with a 2 KiB limit per received combined Set-Cookie header.
  Replacing a cookie uses its host, path and name; a full jar evicts entries in
  a bounded rotating order. Session cookies and Max-Age from 0 through 31,536,000
  seconds are supported. Zero/negative Max-Age deletes a matching cookie.
- Hosts are canonicalized by W's URL parser. Cookies are host-only, including
  when a Domain attribute exactly matches the response host (one leading dot is
  accepted). Parent-domain and foreign-domain attributes are rejected. Cookies
  do not extend to subdomains. Ports do not partition cookies.
- Default paths use the response URL's directory. Explicit paths must start
  with `/`; sending observes the path-segment boundary, so `/a` does not match
  `/ab`. Secure cookies are accepted only over HTTPS and sent only over HTTPS.
  An HTTP response cannot replace an existing Secure cookie with the same key.
- Cookie selection is recomputed at each redirect. Each hop's accepted cookies
  can affect its next hop. HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects are rejected. Complete cookie
  records from a valid worker error envelope are retained after a later network
  error; killed workers and malformed/truncated envelopes do not update state.
- Repeated Set-Cookie headers are split from the transport's combined header
  only at a comma followed by a cookie name and `=`. Commas inside individual
  cookies are rejected. Expires cookies, including normal HTTP-date forms,
  are unsupported and rejected; Max-Age/session cookies are the supported path.
- There is no public-suffix list, SameSite enforcement, top-level-site partition,
  or third-party-cookie policy. Matching host/path cookies can be sent on
  cross-origin subresource loads. SameSite attributes are currently ignored.
  HttpOnly is not tracked as a separate flag: **no cookie is exposed to page
  JavaScript**, and `document.cookie` is not implemented. A future script-cookie
  API must add HttpOnly preservation before exposing this jar. `__Secure-`
  requires Secure; `__Host-` cookies are conservatively rejected.
- Persistence, standard cookie creation-time/path ordering, full cookie-date
  parsing, prefix compatibility and full browser cookie conformance remain gaps.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:

status, `load.address` the final URL, and `load.source`/`load.length` the decoded
body. HTTP 4xx/5xx fulfill; network/protocol failures set `load.error`.

compatibility_evidence.text:

bytes. Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB. The explicit request-header subset
is a plain record of Content-Type and Accept, with at most 1024 ASCII bytes per
value; header accessors, duplicate case-insensitive names, other headers,
Request/Headers objects, streams, CORS and general XHR remain unavailable.

compatibility_evidence.text:
- Binary values: ArrayBuffer, Uint8Array, Float32Array, DataView, shared views,
  bounds checks, detachment, and one-shot UTF-8 TextEncoder/TextDecoder. Unsupported
  coercions and streaming codecs remain explicit failures. BigInt64 DataView
  methods and exact wasm i64 crossings use a distinct bounded BigInt primitive
  covering [-2^63, 2^64-1]; arbitrary-precision arithmetic is not implemented.
- Fetch: same-origin HTTP(S), bounded methods/string or binary request bodies,
  and single-use `text()`, `arrayBuffer()` and `json()`.
  Binary bodies may contain NUL and invalid UTF-8. `Response.json()` consumes the
  same body using forgiving UTF-8 decoding followed by strict bounded JSON parsing. Bodies are limited to 4 MiB
  each and 4 MiB retained per page; text decoding retains its 64 KiB/valid-UTF-8
  restriction. Native AbortSignal options and cancellation are supported. CORS, XHR, response
  headers, streams, and blob helpers remain unsupported.
- Static modules: bounded asynchronous same-origin source graph loading,
  relative resolution, named imports, cached evaluation, immutable const exports,
  and function exports with live bindings.
  Top-level await and async dependencies suspend through the browser event loop.
  Live mutable named exports are supported. This does not implement cycles or
  dynamic import. The current loader aborts its graph on a load failure.
- Animation: requestAnimationFrame/cancelAnimationFrame on Window and the global
  scope; up to 256 queued callbacks, one shared timestamp per visible paint,
  microtask checkpoints between callbacks, and deferred nested registration.
  Ordinary polling/headless dumps do not run animation callbacks; the opt-in
  interactive child advances them on explicit UI ticks. Navigation, tab closure,
  and Stop release queued callbacks.
- Host geometry: location/search and bounded mutable URLSearchParams (query
  strings, copies, pair arrays and plain records; lookup, mutation, serialization,
  stable sorting and live forEach),
  native viewport dimensions and resize events, limited live computed padding
  and font size, bounding rectangles, and offset/client dimensions. These are
  the implemented properties, not complete browser DOM interfaces.
- WebAssembly: validated bounded interpreter, function imports/exports,
  defined linear memory/table/globals, and the instruction subset emitted by W's
  graphics demo. Unsupported types/proposals fail validation; this is not a JIT
  and does not accept arbitrary modern wasm binaries. JS i64 crossings and bounded BigInt arithmetic preserve exact integer bits;
  arbitrary-precision BigInt remains outside the subset. Streaming entry points buffer the response;
  they are not incremental compilers. They require an unconsumed native Fetch
  Response, successful status, and `application/wasm` with no MIME parameters;
  forged objects and overridden response methods cannot bypass validation.
  Modules are limited to 4 MiB and 1,048,576 decoded instructions, with a 4 MiB
  aggregate retained source budget (module and instance copies count), defined
  memories to 16 MiB, and total realm memory to 64 MiB with at most 16 machines.
- Canvas: `getContext('webgl2')` exposes the implemented native GL subset only
  with a graphics context. Headless calls return null. Each canvas owns a private
  GLX context and framebuffer, with opaque handles, upload/draw bounds checks,
  and readback/compositing into the page. Canvas dimensions participate in
  layout; changing the backing dimensions clears the surface. Limits include
  4096 pixels per dimension, 16 MiB pixels per canvas, 16 MiB uploaded storage,
  4096 handles, and eight canvases per realm. This Linux GLX implementation is
  not a complete WebGL2 implementation or a GPU-process sandbox.
compatibility_evidence.disposition: open review; historical claims are not fresh evidence

compatibility_evidence.text:
- Async execution: bounded suspended task records, GC-owned roots, completion
  and total-fuel state, Promise resume jobs and cancellation that unwinds native
  temporaries before releasing stacks. No synchronous wait implementation.
  Async module records expose an evaluation Promise and cached failure;
  browser lifecycle waits for settlement. Native HTTP integration covers a timer,
  awaited Fetch/text, dependency order, delayed DOM readiness and rejection with
  continued later scripts. There are at most 32 suspended tasks, 8 MiB of stacks,
  and 1,000,000 conservative retained root identities. Promise resolution
  assimilates thenables, and `finally` waits for cleanup before preserving the
  original result.
- DOM: stable wrappers survive detachment. Synthetic dispatch reuses the native
  listener algorithm with reentrant calls, preserved event identity, local
  listener exception reporting and an outermost microtask checkpoint. A bounded
  runtime callback-compilation API owns parsed inline handlers across GC.
- Storage: one explicit local owner per app, tab-local session owners. Optional
  `--storage FILE` opens a versioned bounded record under a lifetime advisory
  lock. Mutations use a mode-0600 temporary sibling, file sync, rename and
  directory sync. Failures before publication restore the previous in-memory
  contents; post-rename barrier failures preserve the new contents and report
  `UnknownError`. Isolated interactive execution now routes bounded synchronous storage operations
  to the parent owner. Durable writes run in a trusted helper while the parent
  polls; uncertain publication is reconciled from disk or poisons the store.
  See [isolated storage](isolated-storage.md) for identity, quota, recovery and
  cross-origin navigation restrictions. No disk state is opened without the option.
- Streaming wasm: only native same-origin Fetch responses are accepted; final
  HTTP status must be successful and Content-Type must be exactly
  `application/wasm` (ASCII case-insensitive, outer HTTP whitespace ignored,
  **no parameters**). Metadata survives cache hits, body consumption is native
  and single-use, and user-assigned response fields cannot bypass validation.
  Compilation remains buffered. Binary cache copies preserve embedded NULs.
- Layout: custom properties inherit computed token values, include fallback
  edges in cycle detection and preserve invalid-at-computed-value semantics.
  Flexible allocation is shared between row and column axes; final heights
  reach nested descendants before paint/hit geometry is produced. Reference
  renders compare native pixels with equivalent explicit CSS.
- Frame IPC: `WINT0001` retains the legacy HTML message and adds an atomic
  snapshot/canvas manifest. WFRM v1 transports bounded RGBA8 surfaces with
  generation/sequence validation and matching acknowledgments. Parent polling
  moves at most 64 KiB in either direction and presents completed generations
  without a parent script realm. Integrated acceptance passed 36 painted frames
  with 36 pixel changes, resize, three worker lifetimes, crash/reap, partial
  cancellation and descriptor cleanup. See [the protocol](isolated-graphics.md).
  Raw pointer/key forwarding and parent-owned shared storage are integrated.
  The offline sandbox is now integrated, retaining the documented desktop/GPU
  authority and rejecting network access.
